conviction_note: Q3 is a pre-guided quarter (management said on 2026-07-23 that Q3 consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth would be low-single-digit, like Q2), so the print turns on whether the FY 'mid-single-digit EBITDA growth' outlook holds, which by the company's own reported numbers needs Q4 EBITDA up roughly 8-12% y/y; a record-late hurricane season argues against that, while Hurricane Isaias (Cat 2, Destin FL, 2026-10-09) and Travelers' Q3 hail/wind cat losses argue for it. The evidence nets close to zero (impact_sum -0.7), so p_up is 49. abs_move is 5.5 because the last two real prints moved -7.4% (guide cut, 2026-07-23) and about +5.8% (Feb 2026, TSX). The two numbers agree in sign and both are small.
bar: Revenue: Benzinga consensus about $1.50B for Q3 2026, with adjusted EPS of $1.84-1.85 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FSV/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet; the page returned 403). Wealthawesome/other aggregators give $1.76 EPS, which looks like the prior-year actual, so the bar is DISPUTED and the findings that depend on it are capped small. The company's own bar comes from the Q2 call (2026-07-23): Q3 consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth 'similar to the second quarter in the low-single-digit range'. Against Q3 2025 revenue of $1,447.6M and adjusted EBITDA of $164.8M (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/10/23/3171936/36351/en/FirstService-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results.html), that implies about $1.48-1.49B of revenue and about $168-170M of EBITDA. The FY2026 guide is 'mid-single-digit annual EBITDA growth over 2025' (FY2025 was $562.8M), cut in July from the high-single-digit growth guided in February.
positioning_check: Short interest was 865,033 shares, 1.98% of float, with 3.9 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 3.5% from 835,655 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/FSV/short-interest/, FINRA data published 2026-10-09). Not a crowded short. There is no usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided, 476 total OI), so there is no skew and no implied move. One aggregator snippet quoted an options-implied earnings move of +/-7.21%, but its source is unverifiable and it is not used. Tape: +5.74% over 5 days and +6.63% over 20 days into the print, 25% below the 52-week high and 10% above the low. The NCIB/ASPP buyback is a steady bid (an ASPP lets it buy through the blackout).

findings.finding: Management's own Q3 guide (from the 2026-07-23 call) is consolidated revenue and EBITDA growth 'similar to Q2 in the low-single-digit range'. Q2 grew 2% (revenue $1,449.2M against $1,415.7M). On Q3 2025 revenue of $1,447.6M that implies roughly $1.48-1.49B, below the roughly $1.50B (+3.6%) Benzinga consensus. The likely outcome is a slight revenue miss against the street with EBITDA in line, the same pattern as Q2, when a pre-print consensus of $1.48B (+6%) met an actual $1.449B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-23): revenue +2% against a street expecting +6%, EPS beat ($1.75 against about $1.70), FY EBITDA guide cut. The stock fell 7.41% on the day, but the cut guide, not the revenue line, was the likely driver. Q1 2026 (2026-04-23): revenue +5%, EBITDA +2%, stock -0.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were holding the company's low-single-digit guide, the revenue consensus would sit near $1.48B, not $1.50B. The single-source consensus may simply be stale or carry acquisition revenue. Because the bar is disputed and the quarter was pre-guided, the size is capped small.
findings.independence: The Q2 actual against the pre-print consensus (https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/1101461422, dated 2026-07-16: consensus $1.48B; actual $1,449.2M per https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001637810/000117184326004850/exh_991.htm) shows the street running ahead of this company's revenue before. Different documents, same direction.

findings.finding: Shares outstanding were 43,669,770 at 2026-08-12 (6-K NCIB notice), after 2,311,991 shares were bought under the 2025-26 NCIB at an average of $136.87, including about 1.8M (about $250M) in Q2 alone. An ASPP effective 2026-08-26 lets the company keep buying through blackouts, and the stock traded about $130-140 in Q3. A share count roughly 4% lower y/y means low-single-digit EBITDA growth still converts to about +5% adjusted EPS, which supports the $1.84 EPS consensus being met or slightly beaten despite higher interest on net debt that rose to 1.8x.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the EPS beat ($1.75 against about $1.70) was overwhelmed by the guide cut, and the stock fell 7.41%. The EPS line has not been what this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The buyback is public, and consensus EPS of $1.84 (+4.5% y/y) already roughly embeds it. What is not public is how much the ASPP bought in Q3 at the low prices. A larger Q3 buyback would show up as an EPS beat on a flat EBITDA line. Mostly priced, so sized small.
findings.independence: Q2 call: 1.8M shares bought at $135.91, with buybacks to resume after the blackout and the CFO comfortable at 2.5x leverage (https://www.webull.com/news/15277643593688064). This is the same company's disclosures, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide of 'mid-single-digit annual EBITDA growth over 2025' ($562.8M) requires an H2 ramp that the reported numbers make steep. H1 2026 EBITDA was $267.4M ($105.7M Q1 + $161.7M Q2), against $260.4M in H1 2025 (+2.7%). At +3% in Q3 (about $170M), FY +4-5% (about $585-591M) needs Q4 EBITDA of about $148-154M, against $137.6M in Q4 2025, i.e. +8% to +12%. Management already cut the FY guide once (from high-single-digit in Feb to mid-single-digit in July), and the 2026 hurricane season was record-late (no Atlantic hurricane by 2026-09-11, NOAA lowered its forecast on El Niño), so a second trim to 'low-to-mid single digit' is a live risk on the line this stock trades on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-23: the FY EBITDA guide was cut from high-single-digit to mid-single-digit growth and the stock fell 7.41% (baseline, volume-confirmed bmo). Feb 2026: an FY guide of high-single-digit growth with H2 acceleration, and the stock rose about 5.8% on the TSX (https://www.itiger.com/news/1116490136). Guidance is the line this stock moves on.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 25% off its high, so a good part of the disappointment is in the price, and it has run +5.7% in five days into the print, which would not happen if a second cut were widely expected. The Q4-implied acceleration is arithmetic on the company's own numbers that no preview I found spells out. Inference, not a document stating the risk, so sized below the -7.4% the last cut produced.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 EBITDA of $105.7M (https://www.financialcontent.com/article/gnwcq-2026-4-23-firstservice-reports-first-quarter-results); FY2025 $562.8M and Q4 2025 $137.6M (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/02/04/firstservice-fsv-q4-2025-earnings-transcript/); record-late hurricane season (https://www.ksat.com/weather/2026/09/02/could-the-2026-hurricane-season-beat-a-record-possibly/). Offset in part by the next finding, which bears on the same Q4 line.

findings.finding: Two storm data points after the company last spoke support the Q4 restoration ramp that the FY guide needs. Hurricane Isaias, the season's first hurricane, made landfall as a Category 2 near Destin, Florida on 2026-10-09, with more than 471,000 customers without power across Florida and Alabama. Travelers' Q3 2026 catastrophe losses rose to $538M from $302M, driven by severe wind and hail across multiple states. Management guided restoration to about +5% in H2 excluding storms, said storm activity 'could add to the backlog and improve this growth outlook', and is lapping a Q4 2025 with under 2% of restoration revenue from named storms. That gives it grounds to hold the FY guide and talk up Q4 and 2027 restoration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Restoration storm swings drove the Q4 2025 organic decline of -7% in Brands (lapping $60M of storm revenue) and the Q3 2025 restoration decline of -7%. The stock's reactions on those prints are not in the baseline, and I could not source them.
findings.why_not_priced: The 5-day +5.7% run-up (from about $130.8 on 10-13) may be the market pricing this already. Weather-to-company transmission is not confirmed by the company, and scoping and insurance delays mean much of the revenue lands in 2027. If fully priced there would be no residual. This is a proxy, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Travelers Q3 2026 8-K, catastrophe losses primarily from severe wind and hail storms in multiple states (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000086312/000008631226000180/a991pressrelease93026.htm; $538M against $302M per https://www.reinsurancene.ws/travelers-q326-net-income-rises-despite-higher-cat-losses-but-9m-cat-toll-down-considerably/). Different issuer and document. Management's storm-sensitivity comment is at https://www.webull.com/news/15277643593688064.

findings.finding: Roofing (Roofing Corp of America) was guided on the Q2 call to Q3 revenue 'down slightly with organic growth off in the mid single-digit range', in a market 'unlikely to improve materially in the near term'. Owens Corning guided Q3 asphalt roofing market shipments down high-single-digit, citing heavy Q2 distributor stocking. Carlisle's Q2 CCM grew +8% organically on solid reroof demand, but Carlisle does not report until 2026-10-26 or later. The industry backdrop supports the guided decline rather than a surprise; the item lands inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: roofing -10% organic, 'lower than our expectation', and the stock fell 7.41% alongside the guide cut. Q3 2025: roofing weakness contributed to a post-earnings selloff that drew CIBC to cut its target (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/firstservice-price-target-lowered-to-216-from-225-at-cibc-thefly, 2025-10-24).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the decline is inside the company's guide. The residual risk is a second miss against the company's own expectation, as in Q2, when half the miss came from delayed reroof jobs.
findings.independence: Q2 call guidance (https://www.webull.com/news/15277643593688064). Owens Corning's Q2 call highlights (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/owens-corning-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-08/) say H2 roofing demand is 'much more dependent on storm demand'. The OC release is the source above; OC is a residential-shingle proxy for a mostly commercial roofer.

findings.finding: The stock ran +5.74% over the 5 sessions into the print (from about $130.81 on 2026-10-13 to $138.16) after falling about 8% in the month to 10-07. That raises the bar into a quarter that was pre-guided as low-single-digit growth, on a name whose last print fell 7.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-23: the stock sold off 7.41% from a level that had held up into the print. There is no clean run-up history for the other prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself price, so this is a statement about where the bar now sits, not unpriced information. Short interest of 2% does not suggest a squeeze. Small.
findings.independence: The sealed baseline tape: run_up_5d_pct 5.74, pct_from_52w_high -25.33. The Yahoo quote of $130.81 at the 10-13 close is from a search snippet (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/FSV/analysis/).

findings.finding: Century Fire Protection was guided to '10% plus' y/y growth in Q3 and Q4, helped by the GSC Fire & Security (Austin) and Titan Fire Protection (Tampa) acquisitions announced 2026-05-28, with backlog up sequentially. This is the steady offset inside Brands and lands inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Century has grown 10%+ for several quarters (Q4 2025, Q2 2026) without that line moving the stock; the stock has traded on roofing, restoration and the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, because it is inside the guide. It is filed so that the negative roofing finding is read net of the segment that offsets it (lesson 9).
findings.independence: Q2 call Century outlook (https://www.webull.com/news/15277643593688064). Same company.

outside_window.finding: Restoration large-loss backlog signed late in Q2 converts over 12-18 months, and Hurricane Isaias claims convert mostly in Q4 2026 to 2027. Management said the bigger impact is expected in 2027. The revenue itself lands after the window; only the commentary lands inside it, which is filed as a finding above.
Carlisle (CCM) Q3 2026 results, a commercial reroof read-through for RCA, are expected 2026-10-26 to 10-28, after FSV's exit window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The +5.7% 5-day run-up into a pre-guided low-growth quarter leans slightly against a positive surprise, while the deep 25% drawdown from the high means much of the July guide-cut disappointment is already in the price. The evidence nets to roughly zero, which agrees with a 50/50 tape.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: single-source $1.50B / $1.84 against another source's $1.76): revenue-miss finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4, and the bar field states the cap.
Rule 5 / 'what has worked' (weather-to-company transmission is a proxy and the least reliable kind of finding): Isaias/Travelers storm finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6.
Rule 5 (inference rather than a document stating the risk): the Q4-hurdle guidance finding, which is my arithmetic on company numbers, cut from -1.0 to -0.8.

Lesson 'a reaction history built from the wrong events is worse than none': rebuilt the base rate from confirmed releases (-7.41% on 2026-07-23, -0.27% on 2026-04-23, about +5.8% in Feb 2026) instead of the baseline's 1.82% median from 6-K matches; with rule 8 on understatement, abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 5.5.

Rules 3 and 9 checked: the Q4-hurdle and storm findings both bear on the Q4 outlook but can both be true (a high hurdle, partly met by storms), so they are kept separate with opposite signs; the roofing negative is sized net of Century Fire, which is filed. No sign changes.
